prompt: A pizza has radius $9$ inches. One slice is cut with a central angle of $40^\circ$. What is the perimeter all the way around that slice — the two straight cuts plus the curved crust — in inches, rounded to the nearest tenth?
hint: Walk around the slice: out along one cut, along the crust, back along the other cut. That is three pieces.

hints.text: Walk around the slice: out along one cut, along the crust, back along the other cut. That is three pieces.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a half pizza of radius $2$: the two straight cuts total $4$, and the crust is $\frac{180}{360} \times 2\pi(2) = 2\pi \approx 6.3$, for about $10.3$ in. Two radii plus the arc, every time.
The two straight cuts are radii: $9 + 9 = 18$ in. The crust is an arc: $\frac{40}{360} \times 2\pi(9)$.
Arc $= \frac{1}{9} \times 18\pi = 2\pi \approx 6.3$ in, so the perimeter is $18 + 6.3 = 24.3$ in.

explanation: The two straight edges of the slice are radii, contributing $9 + 9 = 18$ inches.
The crust is a $40^\circ$ arc: $\frac{40}{360} \times 2\pi(9) = \frac{1}{9}(18\pi) = 2\pi \approx 6.28$ inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: Trace it with your finger
steps: Start at the pizza's center, slide out $9$ in to the crust, curve $6.3$ in along the edge, then slide $9$ in back to the center.
Add the three legs of that trip: $9 + 6.3 + 9 = 24.3$ inches.

alternativeExplanations.title: ⚠️ The trap here
steps: Choice A, $6.3$, is the arc alone — the answer of someone who read "perimeter" but computed only the crust. Choice B, $18.0$, is the opposite mistake: the straight cuts with no crust.
Perimeter means the ENTIRE boundary. Before computing, trace the outline with your finger and count how many separate pieces you crossed; here there are three, so your sum needs three terms.
